verdict.rationale: Restate has a dedicated AI-agents use case with docs explicitly describing durable agent loops: every LLM call, tool execution, and routing decision is durably persisted, with automatic retries of transient errors like rate limits and recovery of prior progress after crashes (restate-docs-15, restate-docs-17). Concrete primitives back this up: ctx.run wraps non-deterministic steps (LLM/tool calls) into the execution log with customizable retries (restate-docs-18, restate-docs-19), terminal errors handle non-retryable failures (restate-docs-22), durable timers/external events support human-in-the-loop and long-running coordination (restate-docs-5, restate-docs-6, restate-docs-20), and flow-control lets builders cap concurrent LLM/API spend (restate-docs-11). Community evidence corroborates real deployment experience (restate-comm-1, restate-comm-9) though it's not agent-loop-specific. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on evidence specifically of an LLM agent loop surviving a mid-run crash (evidence is vendor docs plus general durable-execution community use, not a third-party agent-crash-recovery case study).
